items.title: Dreamtonics Completes Its Trilogy With Instrument X
items.headline: Dreamtonics Completes Its Trilogy With Instrument X
items.excerpt: Dreamtonics completes its trilogy with Instrument X, a neural acoustic modelling platform for orchestral instruments that swaps multi-gigabyte sample libraries for a trained model. It joins Synthesizer V and Vocoflex as the Tokyo company's third neural instrument.

items.title: FL Studio says GenAI can help people 'get into music-making'
items.headline: FL Studio says GenAI can help people 'get into music-making'
items.excerpt: Generative-AI music tools can be a powerful funnel for bringing complete beginners into human music-making, according to the CEO and CTO of Image-Line, the company behind DAW FL Studio. They frame prompt tools as an on-ramp to the DAW rather than a replacement for it.

items.title: Songscription talks AI and music publishing: 'We need to work alongside the industry'
items.headline: Songscription talks AI and music publishing: 'We need to work alongside the industry'
items.excerpt: Startup Songscription turns recordings into playable sheet music with automatic music transcription, and is now pitching that engine to publishers rather than around them. Its founders argue transcription AI is the cooperative end of the music-AI spectrum.

items.title: Suno pulls unapproved Mary J. Blige ad campaign citing deception
items.headline: Suno pulls unapproved Mary J. Blige ad campaign citing deception
items.excerpt: An ad campaign showing Mary J. Blige endorsing AI-music platform Suno was pulled within hours after it emerged she had not approved it. Suno blamed a marketing partner for the deception, in a week where its artist relations are already under scrutiny.

items.title: Accentize Chameleon wins Emmy Award
items.headline: Accentize Chameleon wins Emmy Award
items.excerpt: Accentize has received an Engineering, Science & Technology Emmy Award for Chameleon, a plug-in that uses machine learning to automatically match the reverb characteristics of one recording to another. The tool has become a staple of dialogue post-production for film and TV.

items.title: The Three Tasks AI Can Take Off Every Artist's Plate
items.headline: The Three Tasks AI Can Take Off Every Artist's Plate
items.excerpt: The future of the music business is not human vs. machine — it's artists and pros building careers around automating the tasks that were never worth their time. The piece names three concrete workflow chores to hand over first.

items.title: Is AI Slop Giving Artists and Creators a New Life?
items.headline: Is AI Slop Giving Artists and Creators a New Life?
items.excerpt: Growing fatigue with gen-AI content is renewing demand for human creativity, giving musicians an opening to build audience trust and attention. Scarcity of the visibly human is becoming a marketing asset.

items.title: SOCAN Sues Suno Over Alleged Copyright Infringement
items.headline: SOCAN Sues Suno Over Alleged Copyright Infringement
items.excerpt: Canadian rights organisation SOCAN has filed a copyright infringement suit against Suno in the Federal Court of Canada, identifying 150 Suno-generated tracks it says reproduce works in its repertoire. It is the first Canadian collecting-society action against a generative music platform.

items.title: Latest Suno lawsuit accuses AI company of violating the publicity rights of musicians rather than infringing their copyrights
items.headline: Latest Suno lawsuit accuses AI company of violating the publicity rights of musicians rather than infringing their copyrights
items.excerpt: A group of musicians claim Suno violated their US publicity rights by 'encoding musicians' identities into its AI model' and then exploiting those identities by publicly using their names. It shifts the legal fight from training data to identity itself.

items.title: Donald Trump's DoJ says OpenAI should be able to do whatever it wants with copyright protected works
items.headline: Donald Trump's DoJ says OpenAI should be able to do whatever it wants with copyright protected works
items.excerpt: The US Department Of Justice has intervened in the New York Times v OpenAI case, arguing AI training is 'fair use' under American copyright law. Whether training is fair use sits at the centre of dozens of AI lawsuits, including those filed by the music industry.

items.title: The Sony and Warner music publishers finally get round to suing Anthropic
items.headline: The Sony and Warner music publishers finally get round to suing Anthropic
items.excerpt: Sony and Warner's publishing arms have sued Anthropic for copyright infringement, naming founders Ben Mann and Dario Amodei as defendants over the alleged downloading of pirated sheet music and lyrics. Lyrics and notation are now explicitly in the training-data fight.

items.title: The sonible smart:chain Plugin is an Intelligent Mixing Ecosystem
items.headline: The sonible smart:chain Plugin is an Intelligent Mixing Ecosystem
items.excerpt: With sonible smart:chain, the processing chain draws analysis from multiple instances across your DAW so each channel is shaped in the context of the whole mix. Seven processors share one AI analysis rather than each guessing in isolation.

items.title: Billboard Affirms Commitment to Transparency Around AI-Generated Music
items.headline: Billboard Affirms Commitment to Transparency Around AI-Generated Music
items.excerpt: Billboard has committed to identifying songs on its charts that were made with AI, setting out how it will flag AI involvement rather than exclude it outright. It puts a disclosure standard on the industry's most-watched scoreboard.
